package_info.why_malicious: The report discusses general trends in open source supply chain attacks, including credential compromise and intentional injection of malicious code into popular open source packages. It references specific incidents (Bootstrap-sass hack, event-stream attack) but does not provide detailed code or package-level specifics for extraction.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code changes in popular open source packages
Code execution paths that exfiltrate data or credentials
Unusual network activity from build or install scripts
Sudden appearance of new maintainers or credential changes
file_indicators: Modified package files with obfuscated or minified code
Unexpected scripts in package.json, setup.py, or equivalent
New or altered files not present in previous versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during install or runtime
Exfiltration of environment variables or credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected changes in open source dependencies, especially those involving new maintainers or credential changes. Analyze package scripts for network activity or data exfiltration. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized modifications. Employ behavioral analysis to flag packages that access sensitive data or make outbound network requests during installation or runtime.
